purpose: Measure queued DATA credit at first-completion closure without changing sender scheduling.
method: Baseline/candidate/baseline. Daemons persist through paced and unlimited points in each phase. Same isolated Linux 6.8 container harness and disjoint CPU placement as preceding UDP controls. CPU uses before/sent user+system process and thread ticks; 100% is one core. Delivered rates use receiver sample byte/time deltas. Missing uses final receive counts after drain. Worker/counter deltas include drain. No local build, kernel test or Git packing overlapped load.
diagnostic: Sample the first and every subsequent 64th Open-epoch send completion. A fresh clock and bounded request scan occur only at samples. Only coordinator-worker counters are populated. Same-group ordinary DATA requests need an unexpired deadline and current generation; probes are excluded. Fit additionally requires matching MTU, pacing eligibility, a sample slot and enough window/quantum for the first packet. post_fit ignores actual issuance closure and is hypothetical returned-credit accounting.
limitations: Event samples, not time occupancy; counters include drain.
Controller on_transmit transitions and complete request prefixes are not predicted.
Differing-MTU requests are excluded from fit counts.
Candidate unlimited forward delivery is 3.0–3.8% below its controls; instrumentation overhead is not ruled out.
Seventeen reordered frames occur only in the closing production 21G control; cause unverified.
No independent loss, delay, routed path or theoretical CPU ceiling measured.
